n33af509ab30.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the land-record modernisation programme (DILRMP)?
o: It became a Central Sector Scheme in 2016
n33af509ab30.x: The programme began as NLRMP in 2008 and became a Central Sector Scheme in 2016; ULPIN came in Phase 2 (2016-26), not Phase 1.

nfc97649f557.s: The Andhra Pradesh Land Titling Act, under which the State acts as guarantor of titles, sought to move the State from:
nfc97649f557.x: The Act sought a shift from presumptive to conclusive titling, with the State as guarantor of land titles.

nfd793050440.s: CARD in Andhra Pradesh is best described as a:
o: Drone survey programme for abadi areas
Registration system offering anywhere registration and auto-mutation
Property card scheme of the Panchayati Raj Ministry
nfd793050440.x: CARD is a registration system offering anywhere registration, auto-mutation and registration at Grama Sachivalayams; it is not a court.

n015ce5469d7.s: Karnataka's Bhoomi project, launched in 2000, is regarded as a pioneer of:
o: Computerised Records of Rights, Tenancy and Crops (RTCs)
n015ce5469d7.x: Bhoomi (2000) pioneered computerised RTCs; Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN) is a DILRMP feature, not Bhoomi's.

nfd80da24656.s: Which of the following sets of banks issues Kisan Credit Cards?
o: Payment banks, RRBs and cooperative banks
Commercial banks, RRBs and small finance banks
Commercial banks, local area banks and payment banks
Small finance banks, payment banks and local area banks
nfd80da24656.x: KCCs are issued by commercial banks, cooperative banks, RRBs and small finance banks; payment banks and local area banks are not issuers.

ne7942ff845f.s: Nationalisation of 14 banks and the introduction of the Lead Bank Scheme took place in:
ne7942ff845f.x: Bank nationalisation and the Lead Bank Scheme came in 1969, after the first land development bank (1920) and before RRBs (1975) and NABARD (1982).

n80df39fa828.s: Which of the following is a channel used in Andhra Pradesh to finance tenant farmers?
n80df39fa828.x: AP finances tenants through Joint Liability Groups, Rythu Mitra Groups and individual CCRC loans; NABARD does not lend directly to farmers and payment banks do not issue KCCs.

n9a5a104c2a8.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's Pavala Vaddi scheme, the subsidy on loans of ₹1-3 lakh repaid within a year is:
n9a5a104c2a8.x: Pavala Vaddi gives 1 per cent on loans of ₹1-3 lakh, while Vaddi Leni Runalu gives 4 per cent on loans up to ₹1 lakh; both cover loans repaid within a year.

nindian-economy-29-3.s: NABARD is the apex agricultural and rural finance institution mainly because it:
o: Lends directly to farmers through Kisan Credit Cards
Refinances the banks that lend in rural areas
Is the main lender to MSMEs
nindian-economy-29-3.x: NABARD's main job is refinancing the banks that lend in rural areas; it does not lend to farmers directly, and SIDBI is the MSME lender.

n76bda5de427.s: Which 2020 law removed stock limits on cereals, pulses, oilseeds, edible oils, onion and potato except in extraordinary situations?
o: Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act
Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act
n76bda5de427.x: The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act, 2020 removed these stock limits; contract farming was the subject of the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement Act.

n708f2541649.s: Electronic Negotiable Warehouse Receipts (e-NWRs) are tradable on:
n708f2541649.x: e-NWRs are tradable on e-NAM and can also support pledge finance.

nff4233672bc.s: The Union Budget 2018-19 proposed upgrading how many rural haats into Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs)?
nff4233672bc.x: The Union Budget 2018-19 announced upgrading 22,000 rural haats, not 10,000, into GrAMs.

nd1fde02c7cc.s: In contract farming, farmers agree in advance with an agri-business firm on:
o: Transfer of ownership of their land
Price, quantity and/or time of sale
Sale only through APMC market yards
Permanent structures on their land for the firm
nd1fde02c7cc.x: Contract farming fixes price, quantity and/or time of sale in advance; it involves no land transfer (the facts carry no dates, so a sequence cannot be built).

nc0e8ccc4041.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: AP MARKFED – ₹3,000 crore Price Stabilisation Fund
NCCF – Accreditation of warehouses under WDRA
nc0e8ccc4041.x: NCCF has nothing to do with WDRA accreditation, which is done by WDRA itself; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: Under the presumptive system of land titling followed at present, registration of a deed:
o: Only records a transaction, and the title can be challenged
Makes the State guarantor of the title
new.x: In presumptive titling registration only records a transaction and the title can be challenged; State guarantee and a single title register belong to conclusive titling.

new.s: A single title register replacing separate registration, survey and revenue records is a feature of:
new.x: Conclusive titling keeps a single title register; under presumptive titling registration, survey and revenue records are kept separately.

new.s: ULPIN (Bhu-Aadhaar) is a land-parcel identification number of how many alphanumeric characters?
new.x: ULPIN is a 14-digit alphanumeric parcel ID generated from the geo-coordinates of a parcel's vertices.

new.s: The National Generic Document Registration System (NGDRS) is known as:
new.x: NGDRS is 'One Nation One Registration Software' under DILRMP, a common application for sub-registrars and citizens, not an index.

new.s: In the NCAER Land Records and Services Index, Andhra Pradesh's rank improved from 10th in 2020 to which rank in 2021?
new.x: AP rose from 10th (2020) to 6th (2021) in N-LRSI; Madhya Pradesh was at the top.

new.s: Which State topped the NCAER Land Records and Services Index (N-LRSI)?
new.x: Madhya Pradesh was at the top of N-LRSI, while AP ranked 6th in 2021.

new.s: Since 1 April 2016, DILRMP has been funded as a:
o: Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding
new.x: From 1 April 2016 DILRMP is a Central Sector scheme with 100% central funding; earlier it was centrally sponsored.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of DILRMP?
o: Issue of Property Cards for abadi areas
new.x: Property Cards for abadi areas are the output of SVAMITVA; record rooms, digitised cadastral maps and computerised registration are DILRMP components.

new.s: SVAMITVA surveys cover which kind of land?
new.x: SVAMITVA covers abadi areas only, not agricultural land.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about SVAMITVA:
1. Its output is Property Cards for village households.
2. It uses drone surveys.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Mines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: SVAMITVA issues Property Cards (2.76 crore+) through drone surveys; it is under the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, not Mines.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Land Titling Act, 2022 was repealed in:
new.x: The AP Land Titling Act, 2022 (Act 27 of 2023) was repealed in 2024 by Act 11 of 2024.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Land Titling Act, 2022 was criticised for limiting land disputes to the:
new.x: The Act was criticised for limiting disputes to the High Court and was repealed in 2024.

new.s: Bhu Bharathi, the land-records computerisation project of united Andhra Pradesh, was piloted in which district?
new.x: Bhu Bharathi (1992) was piloted in Nizamabad.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's Mee Bhoomi-Blockchain pilot, launched on 24 July 2026, covers how many mandals?
new.x: The Mee Bhoomi-Blockchain pilot began on 24 July 2026 in 7 mandals.

new.s: NABARD's district-level Potential Linked Credit Plans (PLPs) roll up into the:
new.x: District PLPs roll up into NABARD's State Focus Paper, which is the base for the State's Annual Credit Plan.

new.s: NABARD's credit plan for Andhra Pradesh for 2026-27 is of the order of:
new.x: The AP 2026-27 plan is Rs 5.11 lakh crore (about 20% more), with agriculture at Rs 2.55 lakh crore and crop loans Rs 1.66 lakh crore.

new.s: Where is the headquarters of NABARD?
new.x: NABARD is headquartered in Mumbai.

new.s: NABARD was constituted under the NABARD Act passed by Parliament in:
new.x: The NABARD Act was passed in 1981 (Act 61 of 1981); NABARD was established on 12 July 1982.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT merged into NABARD at its formation?
new.x: NABARD took over RBI's ACD, the RPCC and ARDC; IFCI was not merged.

new.s: In the short-term cooperative credit structure, the District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCB) mainly:
new.x: The DCCB is the district tier that finances PACS, which lend directly to farmers; long-term loans come from Land Development Banks.

new.s: Which institution is the main financing institution for MSMEs, not agriculture?
new.x: SIDBI is the main institution for MSMEs; NABARD and the others serve agriculture and rural credit.

new.s: The Kisan Credit Card facility was extended to animal husbandry and fisheries farmers in:
new.x: KCC was extended to animal husbandry and fisheries from 2019, with interest subvention; extension to allied and non-farm activities came in 2004.

new.s: Short-term credit under the Kisan Credit Card scheme does NOT cover the purchase of:
new.x: Short-term KCC credit does not cover purchase of combine harvesters, tractors or mini trucks; consumption and working capital are covered.

new.s: The loan limit for interest subvention under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme was raised in August 2026 to:
new.x: The MISS limit was raised to ₹5 lakh in August 2026 from the earlier Rs 3 lakh.

new.s: The overall priority sector lending target for domestic commercial banks is what share of ANBC?
new.x: Domestic banks must lend 40% of ANBC to the priority sector; RRBs and SFBs face 75%.

new.s: The overall priority sector lending target for Regional Rural Banks and small finance banks is:
new.x: RRBs and SFBs face a higher PSL target of 75% of ANBC than commercial banks (40%).

new.s: After the amalgamation under 'One State, One RRB' effective 1 May 2025, how many RRBs remain?
new.x: 26 RRBs were amalgamated in the fourth phase, leaving 28 RRBs.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Regional Rural Banks:
1. They are sponsored by Scheduled Commercial Banks.
2. They are regulated by NABARD.
3. They took over the agricultural refinance functions of NABARD.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: RRBs are sponsored by Scheduled Commercial Banks and regulated by NABARD; they do not take over agricultural refinance functions.

new.s: Ground Level Credit to agriculture in FY25 was about ₹28.69 lakh crore against a target of:
new.x: FY25 Ground Level Credit was ₹28.69 lakh crore against a target of ₹27.50 lakh crore (104%); NABARD projects over ₹32.5 lakh crore for FY26.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of rural credit committees and chairmen is correctly matched?
o: All India Rural Credit Survey – A.M. Khusro
Flow of Credit to Agriculture (2004) – V.S. Vyas
Agricultural Credit Review Committee (1989) – A.D. Gorwala
new.x: V.S. Vyas chaired the 2004 committee on flow of credit; AIRCS was Gorwala, the 1989 review was Khusro, and CRAFICARD was B. Sivaraman.

new.s: The All India Rural Credit Survey (1951-54) was chaired by:
new.x: A.D. Gorwala chaired the All India Rural Credit Survey (1951-54).

new.s: Against the agriculture target of the Andhra Pradesh Annual Credit Plan 2025-26, disbursement reached about:
new.x: ACP 2025-26 had an agri target of ₹3,06,000 crore; ₹2,96,764 crore (97%) was disbursed.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's priority sector lending in 2025-26 was what share of ANBC?
new.x: AP's PSL in 2025-26 was 63.28% of ANBC, with agriculture at 42.11%.

new.s: Uzhavar Sandhai, a farmers' direct market, belongs to which State?
new.x: Uzhavar Sandhai is Tamil Nadu's; Rythu Bazar is AP's, Apni Mandi Punjab's and Hadapsar Mandi Maharashtra's.

new.s: Rythu Bazars, Andhra Pradesh's direct farmer-consumer markets, began in:
new.x: AP's first direct farmer-consumer market, the Rythu Bazar, began in 1999.

new.s: The market fee levied in regulated agricultural markets is:
new.x: The market fee is 1%; AP AMCs collected ₹429.77 crore in 2025-26 (to December 2025).

new.s: Agricultural markets in Andhra Pradesh are still governed by the AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act of:
new.x: The AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966 (Act 16 of 1966) remains the operative framework.

new.s: With about 40% of storage lying idle, poor storage in agricultural marketing mainly leads to:
new.x: Poor storage (~40% idle) forces farmers into distress sale.

new.s: According to RBI studies (October 2024), the farmer's share in the consumer rupee for tomato is about:
new.x: Tomato farmers get about 33% of the consumer rupee, onion ~36% and potato ~37%.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the farmer's share in the consumer rupee:
1. Farmers get a higher share for pulses than for perishables.
2. Gram gives farmers about 75% of the consumer rupee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Pulses give farmers a higher share (gram ~75%, moong ~70%, tur ~65%) than perishables such as tomato (~33%).

new.s: Which of the 2020 farm laws did not mention MSP while allowing trade outside APMC yards?
o: Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act
Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act
new.x: The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act allowed trade in a 'trade area' without State fee but did not mention MSP.

new.s: Contract farming was added to Andhra Pradesh's markets law by the AP Markets (Amendment) Act of:
new.x: The AP Markets (Amendment) Act, 2005 added contract farming (Section 11A); sponsors register with the Registering Authority.

new.s: The Warehousing (Development and Regulation) Act was enacted in:
new.x: The WDR Act is of 2007, in force from 25 October 2010; WDRA was set up on 26 October 2010.

new.s: Which body accredits warehouses and negotiable warehouse receipts in India?
new.x: The Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA), set up on 26 October 2010, accredits warehouses and NWRs.

new.s: Operation Greens was extended from TOP to TOTAL in Budget 2021-22 to cover how many perishables?
new.x: TOP to TOTAL (Budget 2021-22) extended Operation Greens to 22 perishables.

new.s: Under the 10,000 FPO scheme, credit guarantee cover is available up to:
new.x: The scheme gives credit guarantee up to ₹2 crore; equity grant is ₹2,000 per member with a ₹15 lakh cap.
